title: Shape masking - rectangle / triangle / ellipse gizmo, Add or Subtract to mask
description:
Third masking method beside brush and point-detect (MPI-361). The user drops a basic geometric shape on the image, manipulates it freely, then presses a button to ADD it to the current mask or SUBTRACT it. Pure geometry - no model, no ComfyUI round-trip, no download. Instant.

SHAPES (three, that is enough):
- Rectangle - starts square, stretch or squash any axis into a rectangle.
- Triangle - same stretch or squash freedom.
- Ellipse - starts a circle, squash into an ellipse.

MANIPULATION CONTRACT (identical for all three shapes):
- Click the CENTRE and drag = move the whole shape.
- Drag a HANDLE = resize or reshape along that handle's axis.
- ALT over a HANDLE = rotate the shape about that handle (the handle stays put, the shape swings around it).
- ALT over the CENTRE handle = rotate about the centre.

COMMIT: an Add button and a Subtract button (or one button plus a mode toggle) rasterise the shape into the canvas mask. Reuse the Add/Subtract vocabulary MPI-362 already shipped in MpiMaskCompositeDialog so the two surfaces do not disagree on what those words mean.

PRIOR ART TO REUSE, DO NOT REINVENT: js/components/Primitives/MpiCanvas/managers/CropManager.js already implements the entire handle system - 8 handles ('tl','tr','bl','br','t','b','l','r') plus 'body' drag, image-space hit-testing scaled by view zoom, fixed-screen-size handle drawing on the overlay canvas, and per-handle CSS cursor mapping consumed by InputController. The rectangle case is largely solved there. What is genuinely new: rotation (CropManager has none), and the triangle and ellipse hit-tests and rasterisers.

Also read docs/playbooks/add-app/ui/box-gizmo.md - the Head Swap box gizmo and its top-left-anchored absolute-source-pixel coord contract. Shape coords must live in the same image-space pixel system the mask canvas uses, or the rasterised shape will drift under zoom and pan.

Mask writes go through MaskManager, and masks persist as TEMP PNGs per (project, group, item) - see memory masks_temp_files_not_memory. A committed shape is a normal mask edit, nothing special.

--- UNDO CONTRACT (MPI-376 shipped 2026-07-29) ---
MpiCanvas now owns a shared UndoStack and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z work on the mask layers. Any mutation of manualCanvas / subtractCanvas this card adds MUST record an undo entry or it silently punches a hole in Ctrl+Z. Layer-wide one-shot op -> mask._recordUndo() before mutating (after any early-return guard). Gesture -> undo.begin(mask.undoLayers()) at the start, undo.commit(mask.takeStrokeBox()) at the end, undo.abort() if nothing changed. READ docs/masking-undo.md FIRST.
Specific to this card: the Add / Subtract shape commit is a layer-wide bake, so it records a full-rect entry exactly like bakeAutoPicksInto() does.
acceptance: Three shapes selectable in the mask tool options: rectangle, triangle, ellipse
Centre drag moves the shape; handle drag reshapes it on that handle's axis; both work correctly at any zoom and pan
ALT over a handle rotates the shape about that handle (handle anchored); ALT over the centre rotates about the centre
Add and Subtract commit the shape into the current canvas mask, using the same Add/Subtract semantics MPI-362 shipped in MpiMaskCompositeDialog
Handle system extends CropManager's existing hit-test / draw / cursor code rather than forking a second one
Rotation is exercised on a non-square shape and the rasterised mask matches the on-screen outline (rotation must not be applied to the axis-aligned bbox)
Committed shape survives a reload like any other mask edit (temp-PNG store, not memory)
Every new mask/paint layer mutation records an UndoStack entry (docs/masking-undo.md) - an unwired mutation is a silent hole in Ctrl+Z
